title: Information-Complete Computational Discovery
subtitle: A K-Field Method for Exact Structure, Residual Inference, and Probe Design
abstract: Scientific discovery depends on retaining the distinctions that a model has not yet explained. We formulate the Information-Complete Computational Discovery Engine (ICCDE), a general methodology reconstructed from the K-Field corpus and expressed as an auditable sequence of structural certification, matched contrasts, frozen transfer, residual decomposition, inverse inference, and probe design. Information completeness is defined operationally as recoverability of the retained measurement record and its transformations. Five layers separate registry, metric, dynamics, readout, and inference. A linear residual-to-probe result distinguishes discrepancies that parameter changes can absorb from consistency coordinates that they cannot alter, and gives the exact number of unresolved directions removed by an added probe. Independent finite calculations reproduce the 27-node Cell3 registry, 49 endpoint relations, a 30-dimensional cycle space, and a four-dimensional affine midpoint kernel. Thirteen reciprocal measurements resolve six metric parameters while retaining seven consistency dimensions. A single-family perturbation produces an exact consistency norm squared of 4/525 in the declared units. Spectral moments recover the weighted relative inverse-gap variance 48/169 in a two-gap example. Schur reduction preserves hidden-state normalization, while a dynamic readout example shows how an instantaneously invisible state becomes observable. Twenty-seven computational checks accompany proofs, counterexamples, signed residual fields, and executable reconstruction code. The contribution is a reproducible discovery method that turns unresolved structure into constrained experimental questions, with explicit boundaries between mathematical identity, computational demonstration, and physical mechanism.

blocks.text: A scientific model becomes more useful when its failures become more specific. A residual indexed only by a fit score says little about the missing relationship. The same residual retained by direction, phase, scale, channel, and reference state can reveal which parts of an explanation must change and which must remain fixed. The K-Field corpus repeatedly uses this second form of inquiry: construct a geometric or operator relation, preserve the parts of the observation that it explains, and examine the remaining structure in coordinates suited to the next question. [K2-K5]

The motivating setting is a research program organized around an oriented primitive cell, Cell3, and its finite and recursive address spaces. A common registry supports several distinct constructions: direct and reciprocal metrics, midpoint relations, endpoint networks, wave or relaxation operators, and apparatus-dependent readouts. Their shared addresses make comparisons possible. Their different mathematical roles make separation necessary. For example, an endpoint cycle, an affine null mode, and a state invisible to a probe can occupy the same finite carrier without being the same object. [K1-K5]

This paper develops a standalone discovery methodology from that practice. Its question is operational: given a declared model, preserved observations, and incomplete access to internal state, what can be established exactly, what remains unidentified, and which next measurement can resolve it? The resulting Information-Complete Computational Discovery Engine, abbreviated ICCDE, is a method and reference implementation. The term engine denotes a coordinated calculation workflow; it does not claim a deployed autonomous platform or a guarantee of finding the true mechanism.

The essential commitment is recoverability. A transform may simplify the representation used for a calculation, but the retained inputs, parameters, and complementary fields must reconstruct what that transform leaves out. Statistical summaries remain useful descriptors. Optimization remains available for declared calibration and hypothesis construction. A frozen validation branch then exposes the consequences of those choices without silently changing them. This combination preserves the diagnostic value of disagreements while allowing models to develop.

The contribution is threefold. First, five explicit layers make the interfaces between structure, dynamics, and measurement inspectable. Second, an exact linear result connects consistency residuals and parameter nullspaces to the rank gained from an additional probe. Third, finite K-Field examples demonstrate the complete path with source-addressed definitions, retained discrepancies, and fresh calculations. The component algebra belongs to established linear algebra and reduction theory; the contribution claimed here is its specific integration and execution as a discovery method. [E1-E4]

The Results contain mathematical constructions and numerical replays, rather than a new laboratory acquisition. This choice provides a sharply specified first demonstration: another investigator can reconstruct every stated result without adopting a K-Field physical interpretation. Physical applications enter through declared coordinate maps, actions, and measurement operators. Their unresolved parameters remain visible as inputs to later experiments.
2.1 A bounded reconstruction of actual practice

We reconstruct the methodology from six K-Field source records selected for their explicit treatment of geometry, operators, contrasts, inverse inference, and reduced response (Table 1). The corrected Cell3 master supplies the numerical embedding. The November 2026 research records supply the constructions and their physical interpretations. Each construction is restated with its assumptions and independently calculated where a finite replay is possible. The architectural outline that motivated this synthesis is retained as provenance [P0].

The source roles prevent circular corroboration. A basis used to generate synthetic spectra is an input; recovering that basis from those spectra tests the inverse implementation. It does not add an independent measurement of the basis. Similarly, two papers that inherit the same operator packet provide a traceable recurrence of method, not two independent empirical confirmations. The paper identifies source-derived definitions, new derivations, constructed examples, and prospective tests separately.

Source identity is recorded by absolute locator, byte length, whole-file SHA-256, and release epoch when present. The master also contains its own canonicalized internal digest; that internal digest has a different hashing scope from the whole-file digest used here. Explicit corrected definitions take precedence over their superseded storage conventions. No claim of exhaustive corpus coverage or independent revalidation of the acquisition pipeline is needed for this bounded reconstruction.
2.2 Separate objects before connecting them

Here D has nodes as rows and oriented edges as columns. Q has midpoint relations as rows and nodes as columns. T maps internal amplitudes to measured channels. The inverse-design matrix is called L below, and the quadratic spectroscopy design is called A. Each matrix is identified by its domain and range so that a shared registry does not imply a shared operator.

A positive geometric quadratic form is not yet a dynamics. In a harmonic model, a stiffness eigenvalue becomes a squared frequency only after an inertia and a time convention are specified. A Hermitian Hamiltonian instead generates unitary evolution. A continuous-time Markov generator, acting on column probabilities, requires nonnegative off-diagonal entries and zero column sums; an arbitrary matrix with a convenient spectrum does not satisfy that contract. These distinctions determine the interpretation of every computed eigenvalue.

2.3 Registry, operators, and certification

The corrected Cell3 basis B has the ordered edge vectors as columns. Its embedding uses ICRS Cartesian axes and the source nanometre rendering. The signed determinant is negative; no extra reflection or reorientation is introduced. For an integer half-width ell, the open registry and its physical embedding are [K1-K3]

An admitted relation has distinct endpoints a and c whose midpoint b=(a+c)/2 lies in the registry. Its endpoint incidence column is e_c-e_a; its midpoint row is (e_a-2e_b+e_c)^T. Each unordered endpoint pair is included once. Positive row weights preserve the midpoint kernel; zero weights can enlarge it.

The cycle dimension is |E|-|V|+c for c connected components. It is the first Betti number of the graph treated as a one-dimensional complex. If faces are filled, boundaries of those faces must be factored out before interpreting first homology. Weighted edge inner products require the corresponding weighted projectors. For the Euclidean convention used here, a cycle current has zero divergence and cannot change a fixed node scalar through accumulation: q^T D J_cyc=0.

The final inequality assumes an integer matrix with N columns and d independent exact null vectors. A matching lower and upper bound certifies the rational rank. A single prime alone is insufficient: the 1 by 1 matrix [p] has rational rank one and rank zero modulo p. The replay uses p=1,000,003, plus explicit sector or affine null vectors. Floating-point rank is kept separate from this certificate.

When Q annihilates constants and coordinate fields, this finite open-system Hamiltonian is invariant under affine shifts of phi and conserves the displayed canonical moments. Boundary terms, external forcing, or added endpoint stiffness can change that conclusion. Naming a null vector does not by itself identify its generator with electric charge or establish its physical conservation law.
2.4 Preserve reversal information and the reference state

A matched contrast changes a declared reversal coordinate while holding the reference packet fixed. That packet includes the laboratory and field frames, timestamps or trajectory association, baseline state, channel gains, and the meaning of positive direction. Two unrelated samples do not become a reversal pair merely by being assigned opposite labels. A drift between settings is retained and can enter a later model.

Using 1/sqrt(2) instead of 1/2 makes the two-row transform orthonormal. Even and odd are parity labels under exchange of the settings; the resulting signals need not be statistically independent. All complex channel values and relative phases can be carried through the same invertible transform. [K3]

Consequently, an odd response does not require a globally odd scalar potential. It can be a bilinear interaction between a fixed reference and the reversed component. Calling that channel drift, circulation, or a physical force requires an additional dynamical and readout mapping. On a sphere, the corresponding geometric comparison must also include the inward ambient displacement of a geodesic pair.

The subtracted q(n) term is the geometric curvature correction. Dropping it would change both the neutral response and a reversal angle. For an isotropic tangent ensemble, the bracket averages to [tr(G_phi)-3q(n)]/2. At a middle eigenvector, a tangent angle phi measured from the soft eigenvector reverses the sign when tan^2(phi)=(lambda_middle-lambda_soft)/(lambda_hard-lambda_middle). This is a consequence of the declared phase tensor, rather than a fitted force law. [K3, K5]
2.5 Preserve the prediction that is being tested

Calibration determines a parameter packet theta_0 from a declared baseline. The packet includes the model family, numerical conventions, operator weights, reference frame, preprocessing, readout map, and the data actually used to select it. Validation evaluates that frozen packet under a new condition xi. Parameter freezing does not freeze the independent variables: a specified response can depend on frequency, boundary condition, or orientation while its defining coefficients remain fixed.

If new information justifies a model revision, the new packet theta_1 receives its own identity. Both predictions and their difference are retained. A condition-specific coefficient may be used prospectively when it was specified beforehand or measured independently; an adjustment chosen from the validation target is a new calibration branch. This distinction allows learning while preserving what a transfer exercise actually tested.

This recursion is an accounting identity. It does not establish that a chosen M_j is a unique mechanism or that the sequence converges to a physical explanation. A component must be supplied by a declared rule, not by renaming the current residual. Coordinate changes between stages require explicit pullbacks to the common observation representation. In finite precision, any reconstruction difference is itself recorded.

For a linear model y=Lc, C_Lr is the component no parameter adjustment in that model can reproduce. P_Lr is absorbable by some unconstrained parameter change; it may still reveal a failed frozen prediction. Bounds, positivity, or shared-parameter requirements can prevent an otherwise algebraically available change, so column-space membership is a necessary representability statement, not permission to alter the packet.

A consistency residual does not sort measurement variation into causal classes. Drift, a missing apparatus state, an inaccurate coordinate mapping, or a new physical interaction can occupy the same complement. All remain information to investigate. Conversely, an omitted effect in im(L) can be completely hidden by a refit. Complementary probes and preserved experimental context are therefore necessary parts of the inference, rather than optional diagnostics.
2.6 An exact residual-to-probe result

Let L map p real parameters into m calibrated measurements. Let N have orthonormal columns spanning ker(L), with d=p-rank(L). The pseudoinverse supplies the Euclidean least-squares representative. If the measurements are consistent, every exact solution is given by Eq. 15. Otherwise the same expression describes the least-squares minimizers and the consistency residual must be retained. [E1]

Consider an additional linear probe S on the same parameter state. Its new information is the restricted map SN. Components already fixed by L contribute a known offset S L^+ y. The added probe removes exactly rank(SN) unresolved directions. Therefore

Proof. The original ambiguity is ker(L). A difference between two solutions survives the added probe precisely when it lies in ker(L) intersect ker(S). Writing that difference as Nz identifies the surviving dimension as d-rank(SN). Subtracting nullities proves Eq. 16. This is a linear-algebra result; its use here makes the discovery loop executable.

An arbitrary scalar linear measurement removes at most one direction, so d independent scalar outcomes are necessary and, with unrestricted design, sufficient. A physically restricted catalog may require more settings, or may never span the missing directions. A setting producing several calibrated output channels can remove more than one direction. Thus the number of settings and the number of independent outcomes must be reported separately.

Without a gain or resource normalization, a large singular value can be produced simply by multiplying the instrument gain. The displayed criterion therefore applies only to a constrained, dimensionally normalized probe family. For partial coverage, the objective is first the rank gained, then the conditioning of that resolved subspace. Cost, timing, and state disturbance belong in the declared experimental design.

For a differentiable nonlinear model, L can be its local Jacobian. The same argument then describes local tangent identifiability, not global uniqueness. Discrete aliases, disconnected solution branches, and changes of internal state between measurements require explicit treatment. Repeated measurements count as added constraints only when they refer to the same parameters or to a specified state evolution.
2.7 Keep the consequences of unobserved coordinates

For a finite Hermitian Hamiltonian split into retained and hidden blocks, use A for the retained block, F for the hidden block, and C=H_PQ for the off-diagonal coupling, with H_QP=C dagger. When E I-F is invertible, eliminating the hidden amplitude gives the exact retained equation and self-energy Sigma(E). [K2, K6; E2]

The minus sign follows because the derivative of (E I-F)^(-1) is -(E I-F)^(-2). Eliminating a channel while keeping only an adjusted scalar coupling can lose this norm and the measured matrix element. Successive exact eliminations at the same energy are associative when the needed inverses exist. Approximation, truncation, or refitting between steps can break that agreement.

Here the blocks are generator blocks, not the Hamiltonian blocks of Eq. 19. The formula follows by variation of constants. It displays the causal choice, time units, and initial state that a bare algebraic Schur complement does not specify. Projection and memory have established antecedents; ICCDE requires their otherwise omitted terms to remain in the reconstruction ledger. [E3]

For a time-independent Hamiltonian, the largest invariant subspace inside ker(T) is the dynamical kernel displayed in Eq. 24. Cayley-Hamilton reduces the infinite derivative conditions to N_s powers. Persistent darkness of the entire readout kernel requires H ker(T) to remain within ker(T). A dimensional lower bound on ker(T) alone supplies no protected-state lifetime.
2.8 What a positive-gap response can identify

Consider a nondegenerate gapped ground state with real control coordinates and positive excitation gaps Delta_n. Let v_n be the control-derivative transition vector. In the symmetric, time-reversal-compatible response sector, define inverse-gap moments S_j. These conditions matter: excited-state signed gaps or antisymmetric Berry terms require a more general response model. [K2; E4]

The block matrix is a sum of outer products of (v_n/sqrt(Delta_n), v_n/Delta_n^(3/2)). Its positivity gives the Schur-complement bound. The pseudoinverse is restricted to the responding support, where the range condition is satisfied by the common transition vectors. Replacing this matrix order with a product of noncommuting tensors would be incorrect. For dimensionless controls, chi has energy units, g is dimensionless, and induced inertia has energy times time squared.

This identifies a moment of the responding spectrum, rather than the full hidden spectrum. Equality means all coupled gaps in that scalar direction coincide; several degenerate modes can satisfy it. Zero coupling contributes no information. The tensor slack has no single universal scalar variance interpretation. Total measured inertia or total static susceptibility may contain other terms; isolating the displayed induced and virtual contributions is part of an experimental application.

Equation 29 requires phase-coherent channel calibration and a shared pole. An unresolved degenerate sum can have higher rank and violate the identity. A nearly zero pivot is unstable even when exact rank one holds. Rank tests, alternative pivots, and retained complex completion discrepancies provide the appropriate audit. The statement applies to a spectral residue, not automatically to an arbitrary broadband correlation matrix.
2.9 Six stages with explicit outputs

A candidate that contradicts a required exact conservation law is excluded from that stated model branch. Its failed calculation and reason remain in the ledger. A proposed symmetry-breaking branch can instead declare its new action and predictions. This retains constructive alternatives without silently changing a premise halfway through a derivation.

Numerical checks are scaled to the object tested. Exact integer or rational identities are checked exactly. Floating-point identities use an absolute tolerance for these dimensionless, bounded fixtures and record the actual signed difference. A production application should use an explicit absolute-plus-relative bound with units and conditioning. Values between 10^-11 and 10^-15 are not a universal guarantee, particularly for ill-conditioned inverses, near-degenerate eigenvectors, or long integrations.

The present replay uses Python in tf_gpu_env with NumPy 2.2.6, SciPy 1.15.3, and SymPy 1.13.1. Small operator evolution is evaluated with matrix exponentials; no adaptive differential-equation solver is invoked and no integration-error history is claimed. Exact matrix identities, independent formula paths, and counterexamples test the interpretations that could materially alter the conclusions. Numerical library versions and the executable source hash are retained.

Each release contains a human-readable paper, a canonical JSON record, and a lightweight abstract. The JSON embeds the calculation script, the complete small residual arrays, definitions, provenance, and the verification results. Code and data are separated logically inside that record. Large source acquisitions remain in place under their locators and hashes. This is compatible with the entity/activity/derivation distinctions of the PROV data model, while adding the scientific roles needed here. [E6]
3.1 Distinct operators on one Cell3 carrier

Fresh construction of the 27-node open registry yields 49 unordered endpoint relations. The parity sector populations are 1, 2, 2, 4, 2, 4, 4, and 8 in lexicographic parity order. The graph incidence has rank 19, hence eight component constants and 30 independent cycle currents. The midpoint matrix has 49 rows and 27 columns, exact rank 23, and the four independent affine null vectors. These results reproduce the source constructions with a newly assembled finite calculation. [K2, K3, K5]

The combined-kernel result follows independently from positivity. A vector in the kernel of the sum must be constant on parity sectors and affine on the registry. Comparing the same-parity coordinates -e_i and +e_i forces each affine slope to vanish. The modular ranks and exact null-vector upper bounds agree. This certificate does not infer the physical action from node counts; it identifies the consequences once each operator is chosen.
3.2 Signed contrast survives a scalar cost symmetry

Using the retained G_phi matrix from K3, the fresh eigenvalues are 1.4293287535, 2.1125450264, and 8.8003364347. The isotropic tangent neutral cost is tr(G_phi)/3=4.114070071533333. The saddle reversal angle is 17.725064614421 degrees. These are source-parameter consequences, not newly measured constants. Six tangent settings at geodesic step 0.2 rad reproduce Eq. 10 to the recorded arithmetic residual.

The same replay reconstructs both members of a quadratic relative-state reversal pair from their even and odd channels. It also constructs a deterministic 49-edge current and retains its gradient part, cycle part, divergence discrepancy, orthogonality discrepancy, and reconstruction difference. The cycle component changes neither node accumulation nor the instantaneous rate of any fixed node scalar. An edge-sensitive readout is required to observe that component directly.
3.3 Six fitted coordinates and seven consistency coordinates

For each antipodal class h=(a,b,c), choose the representative whose first nonzero coordinate is positive. The thirteen rows of A are (a^2,b^2,c^2,2ab,2ac,2bc). They map rho=(R_aa,R_bb,R_cc,R_ab,R_ac,R_bc) into q_h=h^T R h. Coordinate-axis rows determine the diagonal entries; mixed-sign pairs determine cross terms. Exact rank six follows constructively, and q sums to nine times tr(R). [K4]

The source reciprocal metric is recovered from its synthetic q values within 10^-12 nm^-2. To expose the two residual roles, add exactly 1/10 nm^-2 to the first family h=(0,0,1). Table 5 retains the entire perturbation decomposition. The fitted metric shifts by (-1/105,-1/105,1/42,0,0,0) nm^-2. The consistency norm squared is exactly 4/525 nm^-4. Every unconstrained metric refit leaves that consistency vector unchanged.

The signed pattern is the result, not merely its norm. The apparent changes of three fitted entries arise from one altered family. Without the complement, a reader could mistake those fitted changes for a new geometric estimate. Without the representable component, the original perturbation could not be reconstructed. This example specifies why both are preserved.

3.5 A zero residual can coexist with an unresolved state

Let the first two measurements select c_1 and c_2 from c=(2,3,4). The minimum-norm solution is (2,3,0) and fits both observations exactly. Its missing component is (0,0,4). The candidate probe (1,1,0) adds no rank. The probe (0,0,1) adds one rank and removes the only ambiguity. The result is verified by direct stacked ranks and by rank(SN), providing an explicit end-to-end test of Eq. 16.
3.6 Spectral information without full spectral recovery

For gaps (1,3) and scalar strengths (1,4), all in declared dimensionless fixture units with hbar=1, the inverse-gap moments are S_1=7/3, S_2=13/9, and S_3=31/27. The virtual susceptibility is 14/3, the state metric is 13/9, and the induced inertia is 62/27. Their product slack is 64/27, while the induced-inertia slack above its lower bound is 32/63. These two slacks have different definitions and must not be interchanged.

The spectral weights are (3/7,4/7). The weighted inverse-gap mean is 13/21 and variance is 16/147, giving relative inverse-gap variance 48/169. A two-control, three-transition calculation separately yields the induced-inertia tensor slack [[1/14,-1/28],[-1/28,1/56]], with eigenvalues 0 and 5/56. A second fixture with two equally gapped modes saturates the scalar inequality. It supplies a counterexample to interpreting equality as proof of one hidden mode.
3.7 Time can reveal a static readout kernel

Take T=(1,0), H=[[0,0.3],[0.3,0]], and initial state d=(0,1). Although Td=0, THd=0.3. The readout amplitude is -i sin(0.3t). The instantaneous readout has rank one, whereas stacking T and TH has rank two. Thus the initial state is invisible at one instant and identifiable through the specified time evolution. The complete complex amplitude discrepancy from the matrix exponential is retained at thirteen times.

blocks.text: 3.8 Elimination preserves state normalization

For H=[[0,1],[1,2]], the lower energy is E=1-sqrt(2). Retaining the first component gives Sigma(E)=1/(E-2) and full reconstruction vector (1,1/(E-2)). Its norm metric is 4-2sqrt(2), and the normalized hidden-state population is 1/2-sqrt(2)/4=0.14644660940672624. A retained-only probability assignment that omits the norm correction therefore misses a definite part of this state. A separate deterministic nine-state fixture verifies nested and direct Schur elimination at E=-2, preserving the full signed matrix difference.
3.9 A completion identity has a testable failure

For the complex channel vector a=(1,1+2i,2-i), the residue aa^dagger has rank one. The unmeasured a-to-c entry reconstructed through the b channel is exactly 2+i. Adding the second vector (i/2,2,i) produces a rank-two residue. Applying the same completion rule then leaves discrepancy -13/6-2i/3. Retaining that complex discrepancy identifies the failure of this common-mode completion, without pretending that it uniquely specifies the extra mode.

All 27 registered computational checks pass. Exact algebraic checks and numerical tolerance checks are distinguished in the companion. The tests establish the stated finite examples and implementation identities. The source papers provide additional physical branches; their proposed constitutive assignments are not silently converted into new measurements by this replay.
4.1 Residual structure becomes a constrained question

The combined method changes the role of a discrepancy. It first asks whether the discrepancy lies within the current model image, then whether the relevant parameter direction is identifiable, and finally whether a feasible new probe distinguishes it. These are different questions. The tomography fixture has fully identifiable metric parameters but a nonzero consistency field. The two-measurement fixture has zero consistency residual but an unresolved state coordinate. Neither issue can be diagnosed correctly from a single error score.

The rank-gain result makes a practical connection between those cases. A new parameter or mechanism should be accompanied by the measurement direction that would constrain it. Otherwise adding that mechanism may only move information from a visible residual into an invisible parameter. The complementary-probe calculation tests whether the proposed experiment actually changes that situation. A model can consequently become more explanatory without becoming merely more flexible.

This is also a disciplined interpretation of cross-domain recurrence. When several systems preserve the same parity, curvature response, phase relation, or consistency structure under explicit coordinate and scale maps, that recurrence is a constraint on a sufficient mechanism. It warrants a search for shared structure. The inference becomes stronger when a common frozen parameter packet predicts several domains, and weaker when each domain introduces unconstrained coefficients that can absorb every discrepancy. The relevant quantity is the dependency structure of the predictions, not their count alone.
4.2 Relation to established computational discovery

Sparse identification methods such as SINDy seek compact dynamical equations from libraries of candidate functions. They already provide an important approach to discovering model structure. ICCDE can use such a method to propose M_j, provided the candidate library, derivative construction, selections, and residual fields remain recoverable and later transfer is evaluated with a frozen packet. The present proposal therefore does not rely on claiming that conventional modeling universally discards information. [E5]

Pseudoinverse inference, projection-based reduction, memory kernels, and response geometry also have established foundations. ICCDE does not claim their invention. Its distinct practical contribution is to bind them to the same source and evidence record: exact structural constraints govern admissible models; readout specifies which predictions are visible; residual decomposition exposes unrepresented structure; and nullspace analysis specifies useful added probes. [E1-E4]

The information-complete premise should be read at the level of this practice. Every retained fluctuation is available for further decoding; it is not dismissed as an irreducible remainder. Preservation alone does not identify its encoding. A finite observation channel can lose information before recording, and no later bookkeeping reconstructs what was never acquired without additional assumptions. The operational claim is recoverability relative to the retained record, with the acquisition and measurement map stated.
4.3 Compare sufficient mechanisms through explicit maps

A mechanism capable of explaining the K-Field structures must connect the oriented registry to actual dynamics and then to the observed channel. The minimal chain contains a state carrier, a metric or cost, an action or generator, an occupied state, and a source-to-readout map. A shared metric can constrain directionality without fixing the occupation or detector gain. A recurrent scalar period can arise from different combinations of trajectory and internal response. The task is to find the least additional structure that reproduces the complete set of retained relationships.

These are conditional experimental designs, not experiments reported as performed. The tests use different unresolved aspects of the same architecture. A disagreement can select a revised operator, an additional state variable, or a revised readout. It becomes evidence for a particular mechanism only when that mechanism supplies the corresponding joint pattern and alternatives are separated by the chosen probes.
4.4 Calibration and energy accounting remain explicit

The corpus itself illustrates why calibration scope matters. Its continuum nuclear-operator analysis reports different scattering lengths after two different reduced models are each calibrated to the same bound energy, and states the unresolved spin, range, and transition-operator interfaces. That is a concrete example of one matched observable leaving another response free. ICCDE preserves this distinction as an interface requirement. It does not treat successful matching at an anchor as automatic transfer to every other observable. [K6]

Likewise, a signed change of dimensionless phase cost becomes an energy change only after an energy scale and action are supplied. If that scale varies, its time derivative contributes. Claims about useful work additionally require the drive, switching, reset, storage, and load terms. Nothing in the graph-cycle or curvature identity alone supplies those quantities. Their inclusion makes a proposed mechanism calculable rather than closing it by terminology.
4.5 The present implementation and its limits

The reference implementation covers finite operators, matched contrasts, frozen linear transfer, exact inverse designs, supported spectral moments, Schur reduction, and dynamic readout. It is sufficient to reproduce the paper. It is not a general-purpose parser of scientific claims or an autonomous search over every admissible physical action. A production implementation would require validated domain adapters, a queryable dependency graph, explicit parameter bounds, and an experiment interface. Those extensions are software and research work, not results claimed here.

The sources were selected because they contain the actual constructs named in the initiating outline. This targeted sample supports a methodological reconstruction. It does not establish that every corpus calculation already conforms to every proposed contract. The audit corrects the paper and its reference implementation; it does not alter upstream artifacts or promote their evidence status.

The main unresolved scientific questions are how to choose mechanism families, how to compare branches with genuinely different state carriers, and how to obtain complementary probes that are feasible and minimally disturbing. The exact rank theorem addresses local linear ambiguity. Global nonlinear branch separation requires additional reasoning. A universal automated rule for deciding which residual structure denotes a new physical entity is neither supplied nor required by the method.

A useful stopping condition is therefore explicit and local: the declared questions have been answered to their stated scope; transformations reconstruct; rank and symmetry certificates agree; frozen predictions and all deviations are retained; and remaining ambiguities have either a feasible discriminator or a documented inaccessible subspace. A zero residual is not required for this form of completion. Nor does an indefinitely refined residual hierarchy guarantee a unique final model.
4.6 Corrections that strengthen the discovery claim

The internal audit removed the blanket criticism of ordinary modeling, restricted modular certification to a lower-bound-plus-upper-bound argument, corrected the normalization of paired contrasts, and replaced causal classification by consistency projection with a representability statement. It also restored the conditional action behind conserved moments, the dynamical condition behind persistent darkness, and the initial-state and causal terms behind reduction. Appendix A records the complete correction set.

These corrections preserve the central constructive claim. A residual can be a measurement channel in its own right, and algebra can determine which new observations would make that channel informative about a proposed mechanism. The paper supports this claim through explicit reconstruction, exact finite examples, and a reproducible transition from missing information to probe design. Its research value is the specificity of that transition.

Information-Complete Computational Discovery provides a coherent method for preserving what is measured while progressively constraining what explains it. The K-Field corpus supplies concrete examples of the required distinctions: a common registry supports different operators; even costs retain odd relative contrasts; exact reductions carry hidden normalization and memory; and small readouts leave structured internal ambiguity. Keeping these distinctions explicit makes the discovery process reconstructable.

The central residual-to-probe result states exactly what an additional linear measurement can contribute: its rank on the unresolved parameter nullspace is the number of ambiguity directions removed. The accompanying consistency projection identifies the part of a discrepancy that no adjustment inside the current linear model can reproduce. Together, these constructions connect model disagreement, identifiability, and experiment design without discarding either the represented or the unresolved component.

The reference calculations reproduce the Cell3 endpoint and midpoint census, the six-coordinate reciprocal inverse, the exact thirteen-family residual ledger, and the inverse-gap variance identity. They also retain counterexamples to overinterpreting modular rank, a perfect fit, a readout kernel, a saturated moment bound, or a shared spectral feature. All 27 registered checks pass; the signed calculation fields and executable source are included in the companion record.

blocks.text: B.1 Why the full midpoint kernel is affine

On the rectangular integer registry, nearest axial midpoint rows force the field to be affine in each coordinate separately. It is therefore multiaffine: a linear combination of products of distinct coordinates. Diagonal midpoint rows in each pair of coordinate directions remove the mixed second differences. Applying those pair constraints at all values of the third coordinate removes both the pair terms and the triple product. The surviving fields are a constant and the three linear coordinate fields. This argument applies to the complete open registry with all admitted rows and ell at least one; removing rows or changing the boundary can enlarge or alter the kernel.
B.2 Exact six-coordinate reconstruction

The three q(e_i) values determine the diagonal metric entries. For each i unequal to j, [q(e_i+e_j)-q(e_i-e_j)]/4 determines R_ij. Thus six linear functionals of the thirteen measurements reconstruct all six entries and prove full column rank without a floating-point threshold. For the full antipodal set, each coordinate square sums to nine and each mixed coordinate product cancels, proving the trace identity. Seven independent left-null vectors are computed exactly and retained in the JSON.
B.3 Moment support and scalar identity

A vector annihilated by S_1 is orthogonal to every responding transition vector because all inverse-gap weights are positive. It is therefore also annihilated by S_2 and S_3. This establishes the common support needed for the pseudoinverse Schur bound. In one control direction, E_p[X]=S_2/S_1 and E_p[X^2]=S_3/S_1. Dividing the variance by the squared mean yields Eq. 28. A zero S_1 is a nonresponding direction and is excluded from the normalized ratio.
B.4 What is required for reproducibility

The companion contains the full calculation source in reproduction_code, its SHA-256 in source_code_sha256, and the source map in source_provenance. To replay, write reproduction_code verbatim as calculations.py in a working directory, then invoke it with conda run -n tf_gpu_env python calculations.py. If source files have moved, supply a JSON map from source IDs to their new locators through ICCDE_SOURCE_MAP; verify that the file hashes match before treating the run as the same source-bound replay. The script reads those sources in place and writes only a small calculation_results.json beside itself.

The JSON includes all node addresses and endpoint-center triples, which reconstruct D and Q exactly. It retains the full Hodge current fields, paired contrast values, all thirteen spectroscopy residual entries, both frozen and refitted residuals, the Schur matrix discrepancy, the moment inputs, and the complex readout residuals. These are compact derived records. No acquisition files or large NPZ arrays are emitted. The source map is required for reproducing source-derived geometry; a hash certifies file identity and does not make a missing source available.

The manuscript uses vector mathematics and vector plots with searchable body text. Artifact rendering uses the bundled document runtime; scientific calculations use the explicitly selected tf_gpu_env runtime. PDF, JSON, and abstract share one release epoch, author record, title, abstract, and confidentiality notice. Bundle validation and rendered-page inspection are recorded after the final layout is generated.

introduction: A scientific model becomes more useful when its failures become more specific. A residual indexed only by a fit score says little about the missing relationship. The same residual retained by direction, phase, scale, channel, and reference state can reveal which parts of an explanation must change and which must remain fixed. The K-Field corpus repeatedly uses this second form of inquiry: construct a geometric or operator relation, preserve the parts of the observation that it explains, and examine the remaining structure in coordinates suited to the next question. [K2-K5]

The motivating setting is a research program organized around an oriented primitive cell, Cell3, and its finite and recursive address spaces. A common registry supports several distinct constructions: direct and reciprocal metrics, midpoint relations, endpoint networks, wave or relaxation operators, and apparatus-dependent readouts. Their shared addresses make comparisons possible. Their different mathematical roles make separation necessary. For example, an endpoint cycle, an affine null mode, and a state invisible to a probe can occupy the same finite carrier without being the same object. [K1-K5]

This paper develops a standalone discovery methodology from that practice. Its question is operational: given a declared model, preserved observations, and incomplete access to internal state, what can be established exactly, what remains unidentified, and which next measurement can resolve it? The resulting Information-Complete Computational Discovery Engine, abbreviated ICCDE, is a method and reference implementation. The term engine denotes a coordinated calculation workflow; it does not claim a deployed autonomous platform or a guarantee of finding the true mechanism.

The essential commitment is recoverability. A transform may simplify the representation used for a calculation, but the retained inputs, parameters, and complementary fields must reconstruct what that transform leaves out. Statistical summaries remain useful descriptors. Optimization remains available for declared calibration and hypothesis construction. A frozen validation branch then exposes the consequences of those choices without silently changing them. This combination preserves the diagnostic value of disagreements while allowing models to develop.

The contribution is threefold. First, five explicit layers make the interfaces between structure, dynamics, and measurement inspectable. Second, an exact linear result connects consistency residuals and parameter nullspaces to the rank gained from an additional probe. Third, finite K-Field examples demonstrate the complete path with source-addressed definitions, retained discrepancies, and fresh calculations. The component algebra belongs to established linear algebra and reduction theory; the contribution claimed here is its specific integration and execution as a discovery method. [E1-E4]

The Results contain mathematical constructions and numerical replays, rather than a new laboratory acquisition. This choice provides a sharply specified first demonstration: another investigator can reconstruct every stated result without adopting a K-Field physical interpretation. Physical applications enter through declared coordinate maps, actions, and measurement operators. Their unresolved parameters remain visible as inputs to later experiments.

A dimensionless five-point fixture uses t=(-2,-1,0,1,2), frozen prediction 1+2t, and a declared omitted contribution 0.3t^2. The observations are their sum. The frozen branch asks whether the original packet transfers. The refitted branch asks which part of the target discrepancy a new linear parameter vector can absorb. The source papers provide additional physical branches; their proposed constitutive assignments are not silently converted into new measurements by this replay.
discussion: The combined method changes the role of a discrepancy. It first asks whether the discrepancy lies within the current model image, then whether the relevant parameter direction is identifiable, and finally whether a feasible new probe distinguishes it. These are different questions. The tomography fixture has fully identifiable metric parameters but a nonzero consistency field. The two-measurement fixture has zero consistency residual but an unresolved state coordinate. Neither issue can be diagnosed correctly from a single error score.

The rank-gain result makes a practical connection between those cases. A new parameter or mechanism should be accompanied by the measurement direction that would constrain it. Otherwise adding that mechanism may only move information from a visible residual into an invisible parameter. The complementary-probe calculation tests whether the proposed experiment actually changes that situation. A model can consequently become more explanatory without becoming merely more flexible.

This is also a disciplined interpretation of cross-domain recurrence. When several systems preserve the same parity, curvature response, phase relation, or consistency structure under explicit coordinate and scale maps, that recurrence is a constraint on a sufficient mechanism. It warrants a search for shared structure. The inference becomes stronger when a common frozen parameter packet predicts several domains, and weaker when each domain introduces unconstrained coefficients that can absorb every discrepancy. The relevant quantity is the dependency structure of the predictions, not their count alone.

Sparse identification methods such as SINDy seek compact dynamical equations from libraries of candidate functions. They already provide an important approach to discovering model structure. ICCDE can use such a method to propose M_j, provided the candidate library, derivative construction, selections, and residual fields remain recoverable and later transfer is evaluated with a frozen packet. The present proposal therefore does not rely on claiming that conventional modeling universally discards information. [E5]

Pseudoinverse inference, projection-based reduction, memory kernels, and response geometry also have established foundations. ICCDE does not claim their invention. Its distinct practical contribution is to bind them to the same source and evidence record: exact structural constraints govern admissible models; readout specifies which predictions are visible; residual decomposition exposes unrepresented structure; and nullspace analysis specifies useful added probes. [E1-E4]

The information-complete premise should be read at the level of this practice. Every retained fluctuation is available for further decoding; it is not dismissed as an irreducible remainder. Preservation alone does not identify its encoding. A finite observation channel can lose information before recording, and no later bookkeeping reconstructs what was never acquired without additional assumptions. The operational claim is recoverability relative to the retained record, with the acquisition and measurement map stated.

A mechanism capable of explaining the K-Field structures must connect the oriented registry to actual dynamics and then to the observed channel. The minimal chain contains a state carrier, a metric or cost, an action or generator, an occupied state, and a source-to-readout map. A shared metric can constrain directionality without fixing the occupation or detector gain. A recurrent scalar period can arise from different combinations of trajectory and internal response. The task is to find the least additional structure that reproduces the complete set of retained relationships.

These are conditional experimental designs, not experiments reported as performed. The tests use different unresolved aspects of the same architecture. A disagreement can select a revised operator, an additional state variable, or a revised readout. It becomes evidence for a particular mechanism only when that mechanism supplies the corresponding joint pattern and alternatives are separated by the chosen probes.

The corpus itself illustrates why calibration scope matters. Its continuum nuclear-operator analysis reports different scattering lengths after two different reduced models are each calibrated to the same bound energy, and states the unresolved spin, range, and transition-operator interfaces. That is a concrete example of one matched observable leaving another response free. ICCDE preserves this distinction as an interface requirement. It does not treat successful matching at an anchor as automatic transfer to every other observable. [K6]

Likewise, a signed change of dimensionless phase cost becomes an energy change only after an energy scale and action are supplied. If that scale varies, its time derivative contributes. Claims about useful work additionally require the drive, switching, reset, storage, and load terms. Nothing in the graph-cycle or curvature identity alone supplies those quantities. Their inclusion makes a proposed mechanism calculable rather than closing it by terminology.

The reference implementation covers finite operators, matched contrasts, frozen linear transfer, exact inverse designs, supported spectral moments, Schur reduction, and dynamic readout. It is sufficient to reproduce the paper. It is not a general-purpose parser of scientific claims or an autonomous search over every admissible physical action. A production implementation would require validated domain adapters, a queryable dependency graph, explicit parameter bounds, and an experiment interface. Those extensions are software and research work, not results claimed here.

The sources were selected because they contain the actual constructs named in the initiating outline. This targeted sample supports a methodological reconstruction. It does not establish that every corpus calculation already conforms to every proposed contract. The audit corrects the paper and its reference implementation; it does not alter upstream artifacts or promote their evidence status.

The main unresolved scientific questions are how to choose mechanism families, how to compare branches with genuinely different state carriers, and how to obtain complementary probes that are feasible and minimally disturbing. The exact rank theorem addresses local linear ambiguity. Global nonlinear branch separation requires additional reasoning. A universal automated rule for deciding which residual structure denotes a new physical entity is neither supplied nor required by the method.

A useful stopping condition is therefore explicit and local: the declared questions have been answered to their stated scope; transformations reconstruct; rank and symmetry certificates agree; frozen predictions and all deviations are retained; and remaining ambiguities have either a feasible discriminator or a documented inaccessible subspace. A zero residual is not required for this form of completion. Nor does an indefinitely refined residual hierarchy guarantee a unique final model.

The internal audit removed the blanket criticism of ordinary modeling, restricted modular certification to a lower-bound-plus-upper-bound argument, corrected the normalization of paired contrasts, and replaced causal classification by consistency projection with a representability statement. It also restored the conditional action behind conserved moments, the dynamical condition behind persistent darkness, and the initial-state and causal terms behind reduction. Appendix A records the complete correction set.

These corrections preserve the central constructive claim. A residual can be a measurement channel in its own right, and algebra can determine which new observations would make that channel informative about a proposed mechanism. The paper supports this claim through explicit reconstruction, exact finite examples, and a reproducible transition from missing information to probe design. Its research value is the specificity of that transition.
conclusion: Information-Complete Computational Discovery provides a coherent method for preserving what is measured while progressively constraining what explains it. The K-Field corpus supplies concrete examples of the required distinctions: a common registry supports different operators; even costs retain odd relative contrasts; exact reductions carry hidden normalization and memory; and small readouts leave structured internal ambiguity. Keeping these distinctions explicit makes the discovery process reconstructable.

The central residual-to-probe result states exactly what an additional linear measurement can contribute: its rank on the unresolved parameter nullspace is the number of ambiguity directions removed. The accompanying consistency projection identifies the part of a discrepancy that no adjustment inside the current linear model can reproduce. Together, these constructions connect model disagreement, identifiability, and experiment design without discarding either the represented or the unresolved component.

The reference calculations reproduce the Cell3 endpoint and midpoint census, the six-coordinate reciprocal inverse, the exact thirteen-family residual ledger, and the inverse-gap variance identity. They also retain counterexamples to overinterpreting modular rank, a perfect fit, a readout kernel, a saturated moment bound, or a shared spectral feature. All 27 registered checks pass; the signed calculation fields and executable source are included in the companion record.

The resulting discovery paper stands on a bounded claim: a source-grounded, mathematically explicit workflow can convert unresolved structure into constrained questions and useful complementary measurements. Its next physical applications should carry the same discipline across new conditions: declare the mechanism and readout, freeze the prediction, preserve the departure, and let the remaining structure determine the next test.

blocks.text: B.1 Why the full midpoint kernel is affine

On the rectangular integer registry, nearest axial midpoint rows force the field to be affine in each coordinate separately. It is therefore multiaffine: a linear combination of products of distinct coordinates. Diagonal midpoint rows in each pair of coordinate directions remove the mixed second differences. Applying those pair constraints at all values of the third coordinate removes both the pair terms and the triple product. The surviving fields are a constant and the three linear coordinate fields. This argument applies to the complete open registry with all admitted rows and ell at least one; removing rows or changing the boundary can enlarge or alter the kernel.
B.2 Exact six-coordinate reconstruction

The three q(e_i) values determine the diagonal metric entries. For each i unequal to j, [q(e_i+e_j)-q(e_i-e_j)]/4 determines R_ij. Thus six linear functionals of the thirteen measurements reconstruct all six entries and prove full column rank without a floating-point threshold. For the full antipodal set, each coordinate square sums to nine and each mixed coordinate product cancels, proving the trace identity. Seven independent left-null vectors are computed exactly and retained in the JSON.
B.3 Moment support and scalar identity

A vector annihilated by S_1 is orthogonal to every responding transition vector because all inverse-gap weights are positive. It is therefore also annihilated by S_2 and S_3. This establishes the common support needed for the pseudoinverse Schur bound. In one control direction, E_p[X]=S_2/S_1 and E_p[X^2]=S_3/S_1. Dividing the variance by the squared mean yields Eq. 28. A zero S_1 is a nonresponding direction and is excluded from the normalized ratio.
B.4 What is required for reproducibility

The companion contains the full calculation source in reproduction_code, its SHA-256 in source_code_sha256, and the source map in source_provenance. To replay, write reproduction_code verbatim as calculations.py in a working directory, then invoke it with conda run -n tf_gpu_env python calculations.py. If source files have moved, supply a JSON map from source IDs to their new locators through ICCDE_SOURCE_MAP; verify that the file hashes match before treating the run as the same source-bound replay. The script reads those sources in place and writes only a small calculation_results.json beside itself.

The JSON includes all node addresses and endpoint-center triples, which reconstruct D and Q exactly. It retains the full Hodge current fields, paired contrast values, all thirteen spectroscopy residual entries, both frozen and refitted residuals, the Schur matrix discrepancy, the moment inputs, and the complex readout residuals. These are compact derived records. No acquisition files or large NPZ arrays are emitted. The source map is required for reproducing source-derived geometry; a hash certifies file identity and does not make a missing source available.

The manuscript uses vector mathematics and vector plots with searchable body text. Artifact rendering uses the bundled document runtime; scientific calculations use the explicitly selected tf_gpu_env runtime. PDF, JSON, and abstract share one release epoch, author record, title, abstract, and confidentiality notice. Bundle validation and rendered-page inspection are recorded after the final layout is generated.
